premise: The unchecked concentration of power is dangerous regardless of who holds it or what they believe.

scale.direction: Higher = more unchecked concentration of power.

tiers.name: Constrained
tiers.meaning: Power checked, transfers of power routine.

tiers.name: Hybrid
tiers.meaning: Elections exist but are tilted; power contested.

dimensions.name: Rule of Law
dimensions.desc: Judicial independence, judicial review, and executive obedience to the courts.

dimensions.name: Electoral Integrity
dimensions.desc: Free and fair elections, term limits, and peaceful transfers of power.

dimensions.name: Press & Information
dimensions.desc: Media freedom versus censorship or state capture of information.

dimensions.name: Civil Liberties
dimensions.desc: Assembly, protest, movement, and the treatment of dissent.

dimensions.name: Checks on Power
dimensions.desc: The legislature, federalism, rule-by-decree, and emergency-power abuse.

dimensions.name: Personal Integrity Rights
dimensions.desc: Political imprisonment, targeting of groups, and state violence.

severity_levels.label: Micro
severity_levels.meaning: A sliver of power taken; the subtle, incremental move.

severity_levels.label: Minor
severity_levels.meaning: Erosion; reversible, still within the system.

severity_levels.label: Moderate
severity_levels.meaning: Real damage to a check on power.

competence.note: Competence is tracked as its own field and is NEVER folded into the headline number. A highly effective authoritarian is more dangerous, but competence is not itself authoritarian.

harm.label: Scale of Harm
harm.note: A SEPARATE 0-100 estimate of the breadth of documented harm -- people killed, imprisoned, displaced, or persecuted -- NEVER folded into the headline. The headline measures concentration of power, not body count; two figures can share a near-maximal concentration score while differing enormously in scale of harm (e.g. a small brutal regime vs. an industrialized genocide). This axis is an editorial estimate anchored to sourced figures, flagged with confidence; it is deliberately coarse and comparative, not a precise casualty count.

anchors.meaning: Repression without mass killing: jailings, exile, isolated deaths.
Thousands to tens of thousands killed/imprisoned; broad persecution.
Tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands killed or displaced.
Hundreds of thousands to low millions; mass atrocity.
Millions killed; industrialized genocide or society-wide catastrophe.

scoring.dimension_score: Diminishing-returns (noisy-OR) combination of triggered indicators. Each indicator's severity is read as p = points/100, the fraction of the REMAINING freedom in that dimension it removes; independent actions combine as score = 100 * (1 - product(1 - p)). One Severe act lands ~50, two ~68, a true Extreme ~85; a dimension only nears 100 with real breadth. This keeps a few severe actions from saturating the scale and preserves resolution between hybrids and totalitarians.
scoring.headline_score: Equal-weighted mean of the six dimension scores (each 1/6).
scoring.level_vs_change: Each profile carries a baseline LEVEL for each dimension (the current state of checks, via 'condition' indicators) PLUS a dated action log (CHANGE, via 'action' indicators). A stable absolute monarchy reads high-level / flat-trajectory; a backsliding democracy reads lower-level / steep-trajectory.
scoring.incrementalism: Micro and Minor indicators are marked repeatable; their factor is applied 'count' times, so many small captures accumulate honestly (with each additional one adding a little less than the last) instead of rounding to zero. Accumulation and pattern -- not a subjective 'sneakiness' multiplier -- reveal the danger.
scoring.matching_discipline: 'Extreme' and 'condition' indicators are reserved for near-total capture of a domain. An action is matched to the severity that would score identically for the opposing faction; where magnitude is smaller, a lower-severity indicator is used. This is the symmetry test applied at match time.

review_gate.symmetry_test: Before any score is finalized: would this identical action, taken by the opposing faction, score exactly the same? If not, fix the rubric, not the case.
